Financing inflow from a new long-term bank loan is ₹6,00,000 and financing outflow from repayment of loan principal is ₹2,40,000; net financing flow is 6,00,000 − 2,40,000 = ₹3,60,000 inflow.

Option A (₹3,60,000 inflow) is the correct figure, but Option B (Positive net financing cash flow) is also true, because a net inflow of ₹3,60,000 is positive. Two options are defensible, so the item has no single answer.
Excerpts state that raising long-term bank loans is a financing inflow and that repayment of borrowings is a financing outflow, so the principle is supported.

E1.1 states that for any level of an input the sum of marginal products of every preceding unit gives total product, so option A (Sum of marginal products) is correct.
Option B (Total of marginal products) is a verbal duplicate of A: the total of the marginal products is the same proposition as their sum, so two options are correct under the stem.
Option C (Last marginal product) is not the total product; it is only the increment of the final unit.
Option D (Mean marginal product) describes an average, not the total; the excerpt defines average product separately as the average of marginal products up to that level.

Net financing flow = 6,00,000 minus the unstated repayment, so the key cannot be determined from the stem.

The Articles of Association is therefore the authorising source (option C).

Shares are fully called up at ₹10 with ₹3 final call unpaid, so ₹7 per share was received on share capital. The ₹2 premium stays in Securities Premium Reserve and is not transferred to Share Forfeiture Account (E1.2, E1.3).
Forfeiture credit per share is therefore ₹7, and 4,200 / 7 = 600 shares, an exact whole number matching option B.
Including the premium would give ₹9 per share and 466.67 shares, which is not a whole number, so that reading is rejected.
Share Capital is debited with ₹10 per share, Calls-in-Arrears is credited with ₹3, and Share Forfeiture is credited with ₹7 (E2.5).

Calls in advance are amounts paid before they are due, in excess of the amount due on allotment or call (E2.2), so B matches IV.
Securities premium is the amount received above nominal or par value of shares, credited to Securities Premium Reserve (E2.3), so C matches I.
